   Plan: add greet.sh that prints "hello"

   Context: You asked for a small shell script, greet.sh, that prints hello.
   It goes at the root of the probe worktree. No other files change.

   1. Work in the probe worktree:
      /private/tmp/claude-501/wtph/e2e/repo/.worktrees/probe.
   2. Check that greet.sh doesn't already exist at the worktree root.
   3. Leave big.txt untouched, since both edits to it were rejected.
   4. Create greet.sh at the worktree root.
   5. Line 1: #!/usr/bin/env bash.
   6. Line 2: set -euo pipefail.
   7. Line 3: a one-line comment saying what the script does.
   8. Line 4: echo "hello", the only command.
   9. End the file with a trailing newline.
   10. Use LF line endings.
   11. Take no arguments or flags.
   12. Need nothing beyond bash.
   13. Make it executable: chmod +x greet.sh.
   14. Check the mode with ls -l greet.sh.
   15. Run ./greet.sh.
   16. Check that the output is exactly hello.
   17. Check that the exit code is 0.
   18. Run bash greet.sh to check it also works without the exec bit.
   19. Check syntax with bash -n greet.sh.
   20. Run shellcheck greet.sh if it's installed.
   21. Fix any shellcheck warnings.
   22. Check that git status shows greet.sh as the only new file.
   23. Check that core.fileMode isn't false, so git keeps the exec bit.
   24. Add no README or docs entry, since none was asked for.
   25. Add no test file, since the script is one line.
   26. Change no other files.
   27. Don't commit unless you ask.
   28. If you ask for a commit, use "Add greet.sh that prints hello" with no
       attribution trailer.
   29. Don't push unless you explicitly ask.
   30. Report the file contents and the verification output.
